page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-24-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 24 dedicated vCPUs spanning 12 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features 504 MB of L3 cache along with 2 MB of L2 cache per core. The platform supports advanced instruction sets including Intel AMX, AVX-512, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic extensions. The system is equipped with 90 GB of RAM, providing a balanced memory allocation of 3.75 GB per vCPU, and integrates 1608 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage across four bundled drives. The instance does not feature discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluation highlights notable single-threaded computational efficiency. The instance achieved top-tier marks in Geekbench single-core execution (2309.0), single-threaded gzip compression (36.95 GB/sec), and text processing. Multi-core operations also demonstrated strong capabilities, delivering 46.34 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and a Geekbench multi-core score of 16269.0. Standard memory bandwidth and stress-ng compute tests situated the instance within the mid-range bracket. Large language model execution with a 70B parameter model was constrained by the absence of hardware accelerators, yielding lower-tier generation speeds, whereas smaller models executed with high efficiency.

The presence of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage creates a highly cost-efficient architectural footprint for I/O-intensive workloads by eliminating the latency overhead associated with network-attached storage. The hardware profile is optimal for production database engines, caching layers, high-throughput web serving, CI/CD build pipelines, and data transformation jobs that require balanced CPU performance alongside fast scratch or transaction logging storage.
